groups.description: The family of brands this domain is modeled on: Peasy (Zaventem), hypotheek.winkel, Verzekeringen.be / Assurances.be and Aanbieders.be / Mesfournisseurs.be.

links.title: Peasy — besparen zonder gedoe
links.relevance: The single consumer front door launched early 2025: mortgage loans, insurance and energy under one roof, in Dutch and French — the framing behind the household personas.

links.title: Peasy — over ons
links.relevance: The sourced scale figures: more than 150 experts, 70 offices, more than 50,000 contracts per year, more than 50 partners and 4.5/5 customer satisfaction.

links.title: Peasy — klantenservice FAQ
links.relevance: Explains the referral-fee revenue model, that the consumer pays nothing extra, that Peasy is never the contracting party, and that Peasy monitors brokered contracts.

links.title: Peasy — budgetbarometer
links.relevance: The household fixed-cost benchmark against Belgian averages that starts the fixed-cost saver journey.

links.title: Peasy — upload je voorstel
links.relevance: Free expert review of a mortgage or insurance proposal received elsewhere — the intake behind the refinancing persona.

links.title: hypotheek.winkel — home
links.relevance: 70 offices, 25 banks compared daily, started 2001, the simulator set and project types, and the FPS Economy Economic Inspectorate as supervisory authority.

links.title: hypotheek.winkel — gratis, hoe kan dat?
links.relevance: Why the advice is free for the buyer: the commission comes from the bank's head office and the buyer pays no cent more than going direct.

links.title: hypotheek.winkel — haalbaarheidscertificaat
links.relevance: The feasibility certificate that compares 25 banks on salary and savings, accounts for the low-EPC renovation obligation and is shown to sellers.

links.title: Verzekeringen.be / Assurances.be
links.relevance: The insurance comparison brand acquired in 2021: eighteen insurance lines and named insurer pages from AXA to Qover.

links.title: Aanbieders.be / Mesfournisseurs.be
links.relevance: The energy, telecom, mobile and insurance comparison brand acquired in 2022: per-category savings claims, free switching, 4.6 Google rating from 2,765 reviews and customer-care opening hours.

groups.description: Belgian mortgage market statistics and the regulators and public tools that frame credit, insurance, telecom and energy intermediation.

links.title: Febelfin — press room (mortgage credit statistics)
links.relevance: Quarterly mortgage figures: applications excluding refinancing down about 37 percent (Q1 2023) and 29 percent (Q2 2023) versus 2022, up about 7.5 percent in number and 12 percent in amount in Q3 2024.

links.title: FSMA — intermediaries (credit and insurance)
links.relevance: The registers of credit intermediaries (mortgage and consumer credit) and insurance intermediaries every expert and advisor in the domain must be traceable to.

links.title: BIPT — Easy Switch
links.relevance: The telecom switching procedure in which the new fixed operator terminates the old contract; more than 99,125 switches in 2021.

links.title: VREG — V-test and V-check
links.relevance: The public energy comparison tools for Flanders; the V-check reads the invoice code mandatory since 1 July 2025 — the free baseline the energy module competes with.

links.title: VRT NWS — V-check usage (28 August 2025)
links.relevance: Reports tens of thousands of V-check uses in the first two months after the invoice code became mandatory.

links.title: Wikifin — over Wikifin
links.relevance: The FSMA financial-education programme launched 31 January 2013, with a savings-account comparison tool and IMMOsimulator — non-commercial competition for the simulators.

groups.description: Independent brokers and comparators competing for the same households in mortgage, insurance, energy and telecom.

links.title: Immotheker Finotheker — about us
links.relevance: The closest mortgage-brokerage competitor: 100 offices, 16 banks compared daily, more than 55,000 loans concluded, mortgage monitor since 2004 and attestation of purchase security since 2024.

links.title: Yago (formerly Seraphin) — digital insurance broker
links.relevance: FSMA-recognised digital insurance broker in Brussels with more than 30,000 customers and a single digital interface for all contracts — the digital-first alternative to Verzekeringen.be.

links.title: CallMePower — about us
links.relevance: Free phone-based comparison and switching for energy, broadband, mobile, TV and insurance, part of the Selectra group (founded 2007, 18 countries) — the closest model to Aanbieders.be customer care.

links.title: DareToCompare.be — about
links.relevance: Independent energy and telecom comparator relaunched in 2021 by Evert Engelen, claiming the first Belgian online energy/telecom comparator in 2007.

groups.description: How the group was built by Vortex Capital Partners from 2020 and sold to Meilleurtaux in December 2025.

links.title: Vortex Capital Partners — Peasy investment page
links.relevance: The investor's account: 68 branches and proprietary comparison technology in 2020, Horizon Group, the 2021 and 2022 acquisitions, the academy training about 30 advisors a year, investing through a 40 percent market contraction, and the December 2025 exit.

links.title: Meilleurtaux — press release on the Peasy acquisition
links.relevance: Meilleurtaux (founded 1999, Silver Lake majority since 2020, in Belgium since 2023 via MiD Finance) acquires 100 percent of Peasy; 81 combined offices, David Geerts leads Belgium and Luxembourg, Thomas Vandeville is group CEO.

links.title: hypotheek.winkel — blog on joining Meilleurtaux (23 December 2025)
links.relevance: The group's own announcement of the deal: about 200 employees, around €30 million revenue and about 70 offices at the time of the acquisition.

links.title: VDP — advisor to Peasy and Vortex
links.relevance: The corporate-finance advisor's deal note, exclusive advisor to Peasy and Vortex on the sale to Meilleurtaux.

links.title: franchise.be — hypotheek.winkel (22 January 2024)
links.relevance: Franchise-sector coverage: 63 locations and 83 experts in January 2024 and the private-equity-backed management buy-in since 2020 — the datapoint for office-network growth.
